To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a thin Ti film with a thickness of 36 nm coated on the surface of a side-polishing fiber (SPF), protected with a thin layer of MoS2 or WS2, is an effective sensor to monitor relative humidity.

the SPR of SPF with Ti and 2D TMDCs can be tuned by changing the relative humidity and that the SPF coated with Ti films of different thicknesses protected by MoS2 and WSe2 shows different responses to humidity.
the SPR-based fiber-optic sensors with Ti/MoS2 and Ti/WS2 coatings exhibit high-sensitivity performance, which can be used for humidity sensing in the visible and mid-infrared region.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and fabrication of a novel fiber-optic humidity sensor based on the SPR effect in the SPF with a thin layer of Ti and TMDCs.
the design, fabrication, and experimental characterization of an optical fiber humidity sensor with a Ti layer of different thicknesses protected by TMDCs.
the design of an ultra-sensitive sensor based on a side-polished optical fiber coated with titanium (5 nm, 36 nm) and protected by MoS2 or WS2 for humidity sensing in the visible to mid-IR range.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SPF coated with 36 nm of Ti and MoS2 shows the highest sensitivity of 0.002 nm/relative humidity (RH) at 633 nm, and a linear range of 58–88% RH.
a 36 nm Ti film combined with WS2 shows a better response in humidity sensing than MoS2.
the SPR-based fiber-optic humidity sensors are promising candidates for the detection of humidity in various applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SPF with Ti/MoS2 and Ti/WS2 can be utilized as an optical fiber sensor for humidity detection in the mid-infrared region.
the SPR sensor with 2D materials could be used for a variety of applications such as gas sensing and chemical/biological detection.
the SPR sensor based on SPF with TMDCs and Ti is a promising candidate for humidity sensing in the visible to mid-IR range.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed sensor can be used in various fields such as medical, food, and environmental monitoring.
it can be used to develop a novel humidity sensor that can operate in the visible to mid-IR region.
the proposed fiber-optics sensor with 2D materials has a potential to be applied in a wide range of applications such as chemical and biological sensors.
